title: Product investigation - 123 school
heading: Product investigation
intro: Test your knowledge by typing your answer and comparing it with the correct answer. Then click 'Check answers'.

questions.q: What do you do in a titration?
questions.a: You slowly add a solution from a burette to another solution until the indicator changes colour (the end point)

questions.q: How can you tell that the end point of a titration has been reached?
questions.a: From the colour change of the indicator

questions.q: With which piece of glassware do you add liquid accurately in a titration?
questions.a: With a burette

questions.q: In a calibration it turns out that 1.0 mL of sodium hydroxide solution reacts with 3.0 mg of acetic acid. A vinegar sample needs 12.0 mL of sodium hydroxide solution. How many mg of acetic acid is in the sample?
The vinegar sample in the previous question was 20 mL. What is the acetic acid content in mg/mL?
questions.a: 36 mg : 20 mL = 1.8 mg/mL

questions.q: Which two pieces of data do you need to calculate the content of an acid or base from a titration?
questions.a: The volume you added in the titration and the calibration data

questions.q: Which pH belongs to an acidic, a neutral and a basic solution?
questions.a: Acidic: pH lower than 7. Neutral: pH = 7. Basic: pH higher than 7

questions.q: Name 3 indicators
questions.a: For example: litmus, phenolphthalein and red cabbage juice (or universal indicator)
questions.e: If you have two of the three right, it counts as correct.

questions.q: In which BINAS table do you find the colour change range of indicators?
questions.a: Table 36

questions.q: An indicator is yellow below pH 6.0 and blue above pH 7.6. What colour is the indicator at pH 5?
questions.a: Yellow

questions.q: What is a decomposition reaction?
questions.a: A reaction in which one substance is broken down into two or more other substances

questions.q: What is breaking down with electricity, with heat and with light called?
questions.a: Electrolysis, thermolysis and photolysis

questions.q: Which substances are formed in the electrolysis of water?
questions.a: Hydrogen and oxygen

questions.q: How do you show the presence of oxygen?
questions.a: A glowing splint glows brighter or bursts into flame

questions.q: How do you show the presence of hydrogen?
questions.a: With a burning splint: you hear a (barking) pop

questions.q: How do you show the presence of carbon dioxide?
questions.a: With limewater: the limewater turns cloudy (white)

questions.q: How do you show the presence of water?
questions.a: With white copper sulphate: it turns blue (or with cobalt chloride paper: blue turns pink)

questions.q: What is a precipitation reaction?
questions.a: Two solutions are mixed and a poorly soluble salt (the precipitate) is formed

questions.q: Which precipitate forms when you mix sodium chloride solution with silver nitrate solution? (use BINAS table 35)
questions.a: Silver chloride, AgCl (s)

questions.q: You dilute 10 mL of a solution with water to 100 mL. By what factor is the solution diluted?
A solution of 50 g/L is diluted 10 times. What is the new concentration?
You take 25 mL of a solution of 40 g/L and add water to make 500 mL. What is the concentration of the new solution?
You see a yellow flame colour. Which metal ion was in the substance? (use BINAS table 38)
questions.a: Sodium (Na<sup>+</sup>)

questions.q: What is an E number and where do you look it up?
questions.a: A code for an additive in food, for example a colouring or a preservative; you look it up in BINAS table 45

questions.q: What do you use a sweetener such as E-420 in a product for? (use BINAS table 45)
questions.a: To make the product sweet

questions.q: A label says: "Contains water, sugar, citric acid". Which substance is present in the largest amount?
questions.a: Water (the substances are listed from most to least)

questions.q: In which BINAS table do you find the meaning of hazard symbols on a label?
questions.a: Table 39

questions.q: Name 3 separation methods
questions.a: For example: filtration, settling, extraction, adsorption, distillation or evaporation
questions.e: If you have two of the three right, it counts as correct.
